properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From hxm_program's F-26 (AJ's work session, 2026-09-23): "Either draw them for any kind, or refuse/echo 'ignored for kind=choice'."

THE DEFECT IT ANSWERS is root-caused in fact:related-to-on-a-choice-passes-the-duplicate-guard-and-is-then-dropped-2026-09-23: `related_to` is drawn only for exploratory ideas (#394 scoped the DEMAND, and the drop of volunteered relations came along untested), while #527 lets any `related_to` id exempt the call from the duplicate guard. On a choice the relations unlock the write and vanish.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:

(a) DRAW OFFERED RELATIONS FOR EVERY KIND; keep the DEMAND exploratory-only. Matches what #394 actually decided (a choice is not ASKED) and what #527 assumed (a declared target becomes an edge). No new ceremony: the caller already chose to send them. ⚠️ Counter: relations on settled decisions widen what `detect_defects` sweeps (the F-03/F-11 brainstorm-edge noise class, now on choices).

(b) REFUSE `related_to` ON A NON-EXPLORATORY DECISION, naming `review_relations` as the route. Loud and simple. ⚠️ Counter: turns a caller's good-faith judgement into a retry, and the judgement is exactly what the linking discipline wants kept.

(c) ACCEPT AND ECHO "IGNORED FOR kind=choice". Honest, minimal. ⚠️ Counter: it still loses the relations, and leaves the guard exemption resting on an edge that is never drawn — the harmful half of the defect stays unless #527's exemption is also narrowed.

(d) INDEPENDENT OF (a)–(c): EVERY CONSTRUCTOR ECHOES THE RELATIONS IT DREW. The reply shows the node, not its edges, which is why this drop was invisible; an echo makes any future conditional drop visible at the call. Same shape as the existing rule that a lost parameter must say so.

Whatever is chosen, the invariant worth pinning with a test is the one #527 relied on: for every kind, each id that exempted the duplicate guard is an edge after the call.

2026-09-28, TRIAGE NOTE (recorded as brainstorming, not as a proposal; no option chosen). A SECOND, INDEPENDENT ASKER FOR OPTION (d). dev_storyflow's wish #52 (art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27, flo2, 0.72.0): "`add_decision … related_to` echoes each drawn edge as a subject-first sentence, like the brainstorm skill promises." MEASURED in fact:root-cause-add-decision-discards-the-edge-echo-its-related-to-computed-2026-09-28: (d) is owed on the EXPLORATORY path too, not only on a choice. There add_decision draws the edges and then discards the core ReviewOutcome that already holds the sentences. add_capability discards its SATISFIES/ALLOCATED_TO edges the same way. On 0.72.0 the choice and no-kind drop that this idea answers still reproduces. Wish #52 is recorded as that finding's proposed fix, not as a new idea, because this node already holds the question.
properties.name: OPEN — when a caller offers relations on a settled decision (kind choice, or no kind), should add_decision draw them, refuse them, or at least say it ignored them?
